## What it is

The LTEE project is the project you build in the hands-on parts of the
lessons, from [lesson 02](../pages/02-project-organization.qmd) to
[lesson 12](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd): the same analysis and the
same data for everyone ([about the project](../pages/ltee-project.qmd)). [It
counts for **{{< event share ltee-project >}}%** of the course grade.]{.content-visible when-meta="event.grading.enabled"}

It is assessed separately from the [capstone](capstone-rubric.qmd){{< event grade capstone short >}}, in
which you apply the same skills to your own research project.

## What you hand in

When you have finished lesson 12:

1. The address of your `ltee-project` repository on GitHub. It must be
   public, because Zenodo archives only public repositories.
2. The **DOI** of its released version from Zenodo
   ([lesson 12, section 3](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd#release-and-archive-on-zenodo)).
   The DOI badge is at the top of your README, and the DOI is in
   `CITATION.cff`.

## What your repository shows

Each lesson adds something. All of it should be in the released version:

| Lesson | In your repository |
|--------|--------------------|
| [02](../pages/02-project-organization.qmd) | the layout from the course template |
| [03](../pages/03-data-management.qmd#hands-on) | `scripts/download_data.py`; `metadata/sources.tsv`, `checksums.sha256` and `samples.tsv`; no raw data in Git |
| [04](../pages/04-git.qmd) | a history of small, described commits; the tag `lesson-04`; a merged pull request, and from then on one pull request per lesson |
| [05](../pages/05-pixi.qmd) | `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock`, committed together; the tasks, ending in `reproduce`; a green *Reproduce* check on GitHub |
| [06](../pages/06-jupyter.qmd), [07](../pages/07-quarto.qmd) | `notebooks/explore-reads.ipynb` with outputs cleared; `reports/ltee-report.qmd`, rendered by `pixi run reproduce` |
| [08](../pages/08-containers.qmd) | `containers/Dockerfile`, which builds the environment from `pixi.lock` |
| [09](../pages/09-snakemake.qmd) | `workflow/Snakefile`, run by `reproduce`; `pixi run compare-to-shell` reports identical variants; the variants section of the report |
| [10](../pages/10-nextflow.qmd) | `workflow/nextflow/main.nf`; `pixi run compare-workflows` reports identical variants |
| [11](../pages/11-documentation.qmd) | a README that answers the seven questions; `LICENSE`; a valid `CITATION.cff`; `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`; `docs/software-versions.txt` |
| [12](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd) | a release (`v1.0.0`) on GitHub, archived on Zenodo with a DOI |

The report gives the expected variant counts
([the LTEE project](../pages/ltee-project.qmd#the-pipeline)).

The history matters as well as the final files: the commits, tags and pull
requests from the lessons show how the project was built.

## How it is checked

1. **The *Reproduce* GitHub Action** on the released version: a fresh
   machine, a clean clone, `pixi install --locked`, `pixi run reproduce`.
   Green or red.
2. **The automatic checks**, listed by the same script as for the capstone
   (`pixi run check-capstone PATH` in the course repository). The finished
   project in the course repository passes all of them once it has a DOI.
3. **A reading of the repository** and its history, against the table above.

You can run 1 and 2 yourself at any time.

## Self-check before you hand in

```{.bash}
# In a new folder, as a grader would:
git clone git@github.com:YOU/ltee-project.git check && cd check
pixi install --locked
pixi run reproduce
pixi run compare-workflows
pixi exec cffconvert --validate -i CITATION.cff
git tag            # v1.0.0 is there
```

And from the course repository: `pixi run check-capstone ../check`.
